title: One PLB L6 over lines approved at different times, or attributed again after a later upload; then interest taken back
assertion: Its entries of each sign never sum past what its first attribution gives it, however many reconciles run and whatever a later upload changes about the claim it names (a claim on another case named later gets nothing), and every reconcile completes; whom each PLB L6 is for is read as of one moment, so an upload during a reconcile changes nothing halfway. An entry is flagged allocated only when its amount is one of two or more parts of a pro-rata split. Interest taken back, by a reversal alone, after a restatement, or netted in one PLB L6 with interest paid, is a negative interest entry against the lines holding that claim's interest, never below zero on a line, and the interest total is net of it. Postgres refuses an interest match without its PLB L6 and claim, an entry past its PLB L6's bound either way, and a line's interest below zero; it skips the reconcile job's interest match that carries only one of them
